item.description: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has intercepted large consignments of illicit drugs in seven states across the country. The states include Lagos, Kano, Kaduna, Sokoto, Ondo, Oyo and Edo, in a series of intelligence-led operations. This is contained in a statement by the Director, Media and Advocacy, NDLEA, Mr Femi Babafemi on Sunday in Abuja. Breaking down the operation, Babafemi said NDLEA operatives, acting on actionable intelligence about the movement of skunk, intercepted a white Volkswagen LT 28 bus along Kudirat Abiola Way, Ikeja, Lagos. Babafemi said the NDLEA operatives intercepted 537kg of skunk, a potent strain of cannabis, on Sunday, Oct. 25, while it was being transported from the Island to the Mainland. “The same day, another team of officers intercepted a brown J5 bus along the Gbagada–Oshodi expressway, with 439 kilograms of the same substance seized,”he said. In Oyo, NDLEA operatives on Thursday conducted a follow-up operation at Idere road, Igboora, where two suspects were arrested. Babafemi said that their arrest came while loading 554 kilograms of skunk into a Volvo truck for onward movement into town. “The operation targeted a notorious drug dealer known as ‘Omo Oba’, who escaped arrest on October 25. “This happened when officers seized 309.5 kilograms of the strong cannabis strain popularly called ‘Ghanaian Loud’ linked to him,” he said. item.title: China’s State TV snubs Real Madrid match amid Mbappé controversy
item.description: Chinese state broadcaster CCTV did not broadcast a Real Madrid La Liga match on Sunday after star forward Kylian Mbappe caused a furore in China with remarks he made about former leader Mao Zedong. The match between Real Madrid and Racing Santander began at 1515 GMT but was not broadcast on either of CCTV’s two sports channels, AFP reporters saw. None of the other matches from the 11th round of La Liga have been broadcast live on public television so far. The rules must apply equally to every political party. The electoral process must be fair, transparent and predictable, without adjusting deadlines in a manner that gives any party an undue advantage,” Yilwatda said. He said the APC had already released its campaign council list, inaugurated the council, commenced campaign activities and uploaded its candidates to the INEC portal ahead of its rivals. According to him, the party has presented candidates for all the elective positions it is contesting, in contrast to the difficulties some opposition parties reportedly encountered in fielding candidates and completing their submission processes. He said APC’s organisational strength placed it ahead of other parties. “Our party is the largest political party in Nigeria. In terms of structure, organisation and membership, no other political party comes close to us. We are approximately three times larger than the next political party in the country,” he said. He disclosed that the party has approximately 13 million registered members in all local government areas, with membership identity cards designed to allow verification through their National Identification Numbers NIN and voter identification details. The chairman added that the APC has more than 261,000 executive members across its structures from the ward to the national level. On elected offices, he said the party has 31 governors out of 36, 88 senators out of the 109-member Senate, and 208 members of the House of Representatives out of 360 seats. He added that the party also has a significant presence in state Houses of Assembly. “These structures are the foundation of our strength. We have built an organisation that reaches every part of the country and gives us the capacity to engage Nigerians across different demographics,” he said. Yilwatda said more than 7,000 aspirants contested for various positions in the party’s primaries, yet it recorded relatively few post-primary court cases compared with the scale of the contests. He observed that several politicians who failed to secure APC tickets later obtained tickets from opposition parties, including the African Democratic Congress ADC and the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC. He said this underscored the intensity of competition for the APC’s tickets. Yilwatda, however, drew a line between size and dominance. “Being the largest political party does not mean that we want to suppress anybody. We want a democratic environment in which every party can organise, campaign and seek the support of Nigerians without fear,” he said. The chairman stressed that the party’s preparation was based on its organisational capacity, candidate readiness and nationwide structures, not on an assumption that victory was automatic. He assured the ECOWAS mission that the APC would not use its position to suppress opposition parties, and said all parties should enjoy equal access to the media, campaign venues and other legitimate opportunities to present their programmes to the electorate. Yilwatda cited public protests against the administration of President Bola Tinubu, including the “Tinubu Must Go” demonstrations, as evidence that citizens and opposition groups could express their views without being automatically subjected to arrest or intimidation. He also pointed to the political realignments that followed the APC’s defeat in the Anambra and Osun governorship elections. He said the party engaged stakeholders after those losses, and that the engagements contributed to broader alliances in support of Tinubu’s re-election bid. Earlier, Foh explained that the mission was undertaking a political assessment aimed at contributing to free, fair and transparent elections in Nigeria. “Our monitoring is scientific, and our decisions on issues are based on scientific observation. We verify information before making any pronouncement, and we use a robust application system to collect data. Our reports are therefore not arbitrary,” he said. Foh commended Yilwatda for his detailed presentation, saying it gave the mission valuable insight into the APC’s structure, membership, internal processes and preparations for the elections. item.title: Atiku tackles APC over Tinubu’s power pledge, says bonds can’t light homes
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, APC-PCC, over its defence of President Bola Tinubu’s electricity pledge, insisting that Nigerians cannot power their homes and businesses with laws, bonds and project announcements. Atiku said despite the administration’s explanations about reforms and ongoing projects, Nigerians were still battling unreliable electricity, rising tariffs and the cost of alternative power, three and a half years after Tinubu promised steady supply and an end to estimated billing. item.title: FG launches USSD service to help Nigerians access loans without internet [How to apply]
item.description: The Federal Government has launched a new USSD-based credit service, SPARK, designed to help Nigerians access loans and build formal credit histories using basic mobile phones. The product, introduced by the Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation (CREDICORP), targets Nigerians, particularly first-time borrowers who have limited or no credit history. Interested Nigerians can dial *347*333# on their mobile phones to access the service without requiring a smartphone or internet connection. According to CREDICORP, SPARK is designed to simplify access to consumer credit while helping beneficiaries establish repayment records that could improve their credit profiles and open up further financial opportunities. “By establishing repayment records through responsible borrowing, beneficiaries can progressively improve their credit profiles and create pathways to greater financial opportunities,” the corporation said. It added that the product is expected to become more widely available to Nigerians before the end of 2026. The event brought together beneficiaries, participating financial institutions, local vendors and government representatives to demonstrate how consumer credit could support businesses and improve livelihoods. item.title: FBI says North Korea behind $6 billion crypto theft from Binance
item.description: Binance said Sunday that it had resumed withdrawals after more than $6 billion in virtual assets were stolen from the cryptocurrency exchange in a major hack the FBI said North Korea was responsible for. Binance is the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes. News of the hacking attack, which is thought to be the biggest-ever crypto heist, caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply on Friday. The company has offered reassurances it will cover the losses from the attack, saying it has used company funds to buy tokens to replenish 90 percent of what was stolen. Binance suspended user withdrawals after the attack but said they would be resumed in phases, the first of which began on Sunday. “First batch network now opened in phase one of withdrawals,” the exchange posted on X . The US law enforcement agency accused North Korea of being behind the hack in a statement on Saturday, confirming earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a Pyongyang-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was responsible. TraderTraitor is the same group blamed for a $1.5 billion theft from the Bybit platform in February last year. “The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is releasing information advising the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29, 2026,” the statement said. The FBI added that it had observed “TraderTraitor actors” converting stolen assets into Ethereum, and expected those assets to be laundered further by converting them using decentralized finance and instant swap services. It said it was urging private sector entities “to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets.” US President Donald Trump cast doubt on the North Korea’s involvement in the hack. “I’m not concerned. We’re learning about it. We don’t know if it’s North Korea,” Trump told reporters at his residence in Florida late Saturday. The president often reflects with pride on summits he held with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his first term. Binance has said that it was preparing to gradually resume withdrawals, starting at between 0600 and 0900 GMT on Sunday. “We are taking a phased approach by prioritizing tokens based on the past week data of user demand, so that each network and asset pair can be restored carefully, with stability and security checks completed before access is reopened,” it said. – ‘Cover the financial impact’ – Binance said Saturday it has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses in the hack. “Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said on X. TraderTraitor is believed to be part of the Lazarus Group, which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for “The Interview,” a film that mocked North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. item.title: Betta Edu courts 500 C’River women, sets 1.5m vote target for Tinubu
item.description: Former Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr Betta Edu, has set a target of 1.5 million votes from Cross River for President Bola Tinubu, come 2027 general elections. Edu, Co-Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mobilisation Directorate, made the declaration on Sunday in Calabar, during an empowerment programme that benefited about 500 market women, petty traders and artisans. She said the initiative organised at the instance of the First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu, was designed to improve women’s economic livelihood, and strengthen grassroots mobilisation. She said the beneficiaries received N50,000 each, alongside business and household equipment, including deep freezers, blenders, and toasters. According to her, the intervention targets petty traders whose businesses are constrained by inadequate capital. “Some of them are selling trays that have just N5,000 worth of things on them, while some of them have trays with just N10,000 worth of items on them. “So we are giving these sets of petty traders N50,000 each so that they can expand that their business, build on it, so things can get better for them and their children,” she said. Edu urged residents of the state to support Tinubu, Gov. Bassey Otu and other APC candidates as the party was banking on grassroots women’s mobilisation to strengthen its electoral fortunes in the state. She expressed confidence that the state would deliver more than 1.5 million votes for the ruling party, adding that the directorate was establishing support structures for women across the country. She disclosed that the empowerment programme would be extended to other parts of Cross River, with Abi Local Government Area scheduled to benefit in November or December, while the northern senatorial district would be reached in January. The former minister also highlighted some Federal Government interventions, including the student loan scheme and free maternal healthcare, as measures aimed at improving the welfare of Nigerians. As part of the mobilisation activities, she led members of the directorate on a visit to the General Hospital, Calabar, where they interacted with patients, pregnant women and children receiving treatment and offered financial and emotional support. She said the hospital outreach was undertaken at the instance of the First Lady ahead of the APC rally scheduled to hold in Calabar on Monday. Edu also cited subsidised dialysis services and free maternal healthcare as interventions aimed at improving healthcare access and reducing maternal mortality. One of the beneficiaries, Esther Bassey, a widow from Odukpani Local Government Area, expressed appreciation for the support, saying previous empowerment programmes had helped her cater for her three children. item.title: ‎2027: Promote peace, policies, not personal attacks – PDP tells supporters
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa Dutse ‎ ‎The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Jigawa State has urged its social media supporters to promote peaceful political engagement, issue-based campaigns and policy discussions rather than engage in insults and personal attacks ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎ ‎The party’s governorship candidate, Mustapha Sule Lamido, made the call during a meeting with PDP social media users and political commentators in the state. ‎ ‎Lamido urged the supporters to use their platforms responsibly by promoting the party’s programmes, policies and candidates through constructive engagement. ‎ ‎He stressed that political campaigns should be driven by ideas and policies capable of winning public confidence, rather than abusive language and personal attacks. ‎ ‎”Political campaigns should focus on issues, policies and programmes that can convince the electorate, not insults or attacks on individuals,” Lamido said. ‎ ‎According to him, the meeting was organised to sensitise youths on the importance of responsible political communication and their role in promoting the party ahead of the 2027 elections. ‎ ‎He further disclosed that the party had completed arrangements to commence its campaign activities across Jigawa State. ‎ ‎Lamido reaffirmed the PDP’s commitment to conducting peaceful and orderly campaign tours across the state, without violence or unnecessary provocation. ‎ ‎”We are committed to peaceful campaigns across Jigawa State, and we urge our supporters to avoid anything that could create tension or disrupt public peace,” he said. ‎ ‎The governorship candidate also expressed appreciation to the people of Jigawa State for their continued support for the PDP, urging them to sustain their confidence in the party. item.title: French School Blockades To Restart From Monday – Student Group
item.description: The head of a student group said a campaign of high school blockades would restart from Monday, adding the government’s proposals did not go far enough. On Saturday, hundreds of thousands of people, including high school and university students, took to the streets across France for a third consecutive weekend of protests. Some high schools will be blockaded from Monday, when students return from a two-week holiday, said Pierre Sourzat, head of the “Lyceens!” group. “It will be more significant from Tuesday, but we know that some schools will be blocked as early as tomorrow,” he told broadcaster RMC on Sunday. “We support all our comrades who are blocking their schools from tomorrow,” he added. A protester throws a smoke flare towards French gendarmes during a demonstration to protest against the “high cost of living”, in Bordeaux, southwestern France, on October 17, 2026 as part of a nationwide call for mobilisation bringing together various groups expressing their anger: former “Yellow Vest”, secondary school and university students, climate activists and even farmers. (Photo by CHRISTOPHE ARCHAMBAULT / AFP) France’s protest movement against soaring prices emerged from weeks of demonstrations by high school students protesting deteriorating learning conditions and inequality. On Monday, the government announced a series of measures aimed at addressing student protesters’ demands, including replacing the university admissions platform and providing loans for school renovations. Students said the proposals did not go far enough. On Saturday, Sabrine Kharbach, spokeswoman for the Union Etudiante (Student Union), said blockades of universities and high schools would take place on Tuesday and Thursday. President Emmanuel Macron has called for classes to resume in a calm manner, arguing that “young people have been heard”. Sourzat countered that “the president hasn’t listened to us”. “It’s smoke and mirrors,” he said. “There’s a bit of polish on the surface, but once you scratch beneath it, there’s nothing there.” Sourzat said the proposed overhaul of the university admissions platform, long criticised for its lack of transparency, failed to address the shortage of places in higher education. He also dismissed the government’s plan to reduce class sizes as insufficient, noting that it would apply only to 10th-grade classes. “We were asking for all year groups,” he said. With the eurozone’s second-largest economy on the brink of recession and under pressure to rein in its debt, the government has limited scope to appease student protesters through additional spending. The publication had expressed concerns about DESOPADEC’s funding and the development of oil-producing communities, while urging residents to vote against Oborevwori and the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general elections. However, Delta HOSTCOM said the views and political recommendations contained in the article should be regarded as those of its author and not attributed to the state chapter. The organisation explained that its recognised leadership comprised Enujeke as chairman and Lamienghan as secretary, adding that official positions issued in its name should reflect the decisions of its leadership. It urged media organisations, government institutions, political parties, oil and gas industry stakeholders, community leaders and the public to take note of its clarification. DESOPADEC payment dispute On the dispute concerning the 30 per cent payment to DESOPADEC workers, the organisation appealed to the workers and management to maintain peace and allow the court to determine the matter. It stressed the importance of respecting the judicial process while awaiting the final ruling. Delta HOSTCOM also expressed support for the objectives of Governor Oborevwori’s MORE Agenda, which stands for Meaningful Development, Opportunities for All, Realistic Reforms and Enhanced Peace and Security. The organisation said sustained engagement between the state government and host communities was important to addressing developmental challenges, improving living conditions and promoting peace in oil-producing areas. It added, however, that its position on the agenda should not be interpreted as an endorsement of every government policy or a dismissal of concerns relating to DESOPADEC’s statutory responsibilities. According to the statement, issues concerning the commission’s funding, project execution, statutory obligations and workers’ welfare require constructive engagement with relevant authorities. It said environmental justice, infrastructure development, transparency, accountability and improved welfare remained important to the development of oil-producing communities. HOSTCOM outlines endorsement process The organisation said it would continue to engage its constituent communities through town hall meetings before taking decisions on political endorsements. It explained that such consultations would provide an opportunity for members to discuss issues affecting their communities and collectively determine their position. The leadership said: “HOSTCOM does not involve itself in campaigns. What we do is organise town hall meetings, which will kick-start soon. At the grand finale, that is when we normally endorse credible candidates, who must be delivered by the oil-producing communities across the 21 local government areas.” Delta HOSTCOM called for unity among oil-producing communities and reiterated its commitment to engaging government authorities and other stakeholders on matters affecting their welfare. It maintained that the disputed publication was not an official statement or political position of the Delta State chapter. But the involvement of an identifiable former local-government chairman establishes that this is more than an anonymous claim of mass defection. The development complicates Adamawa’s political picture. The APC has gained elected local-government officials who previously belonged to the PDP. The APM is now attracting some politicians from the APC. And the PDP must continue organising after losing a substantial number of its elected council officials. But there is an important qualification. The local-government elections that produced Adamawa’s council chairmen were conducted by the Adamawa State Independent Electoral Commission, not INEC. Their results established who was elected to local office. They did not measure how Adamawa residents intend to vote in the 2027 presidential election. Likewise, the subsequent defections establish changes in the affiliations of politicians, not necessarily changes in the preferences of their constituents. The political structures have moved. Whether the voters move with them remains an open question. That distinction will become increasingly important as the campaign progresses. IMO: AN ELECTION POSTPONED, AN OPPORTUNITY FOR EVIDENCE LOST Another development emerged in Imo State. The Imo State Independent Electoral Commission has indefinitely postponed the local-government elections previously scheduled for November 7. The elections had initially been planned for September 26 before being rescheduled. The Commission says its latest decision followed consultations with political parties and the Inter-Party Advisory Council. No replacement date has been announced. The proposed elections would have covered 27 local-government areas and 305 wards. Their postponement means there will be no immediate fresh council-election evidence from Imo ahead of the general elections. But even if the elections had proceeded, their results would have required careful interpretation. Local-government elections conducted by state electoral commissions are not administered under precisely the same arrangements as INEC-run federal and state elections. They may tell us something about political organisation, local participation and the ability of parties to field candidates. But a sweep of council seats does not necessarily establish how the same electorate will vote in a presidential contest. Imo therefore remains a state where we must look beyond local-government party control when assessing the political environment. The postponement also raises a straightforward administrative question. When will residents have another opportunity to elect their local-government representatives? That deserves an answer independently of the 2027 campaign. The Commission received 130 petitions concerning governorship and State Houses of Assembly nominations. Of these, 66 were upheld and 64 rejected. The governorship petitions came from 12 political parties across 26 states. INEC accepted 41 of the 69 governorship petitions and rejected 28. For State Houses of Assembly nominations, 25 petitions succeeded while 36 failed. The Commission says its decisions followed consideration of complaints, party records and applicable legal provisions. This is significant because the controversy over nominations has now moved beyond arguments and petitions. INEC has made administrative determinations. item.title: Nigerians, other foreign graduates to get shorter UK work visa from 2027
item.description: The United Kingdom, UK has announced plans to retain its two-year post-study work visa for international students graduating from selected universities, partially reversing an earlier decision to reduce the duration of the scheme. Under the revised policy, graduates of universities with strong immigration compliance records and employment outcomes will continue to qualify for the two-year Graduate visa, while other international graduates will receive 18 months from January 2027. The UK government disclosed the change in its 2026 Budget, although it has yet to publish the list of qualifying universities or explain how institutions will be assessed. The policy introduces a two-tier system in which the university attended by an international student could determine how long they can remain in Britain after completing their studies. “The government will also increase the duration of the Graduate visa to two years for graduates from high compliance universities where there are strong labour market outcomes,” the Budget document said. The change comes after the government announced plans to reduce the standard Graduate visa from two years to 18 months for bachelor’s and master’s degree holders, effective January 1, 2027. Doctoral graduates will continue to qualify for three years. The development could affect thousands of African students, particularly Nigerians, who constitute a significant proportion of Britain’s international student population and rely on post-study employment opportunities to gain work experience and recover the cost of their education. Nigeria was the UK’s third-largest source of sponsored international students in the year ending June 2026, with 26,060 sponsored study visas issued to Nigerian main applicants, behind China and India. Nigerian nationals also recorded 20,604 approvals under the Graduate route during the period, making them the third-largest nationality group to benefit from the scheme. The Graduate visa allows eligible international students to work or search for employment in Britain without requiring immediate employer sponsorship. However, the visa cannot be extended, and graduates seeking to remain longer must switch to another eligible immigration route, such as the Skilled Worker visa. Students graduating before the end of 2026 can still apply for the existing two-year Graduate visa, while the reduced 18-month duration will apply to applications submitted from January 1, 2027. hile maintaining opportunities for international graduates and professionals considered valuable to the country’s labour market. item.title: Delta reduces inherited debt by N400bn, targets 2027 clearance
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi ASABA — The Delta State Government says it has reduced the state’s inherited debt from N463 billion to N63 billion and is targeting full repayment of the outstanding balance by the first quarter of 2027. The Commissioner for Economic Planning, Mr Sonny Ekedayen, disclosed this at the 2026 budget stakeholders’ engagement held in Asaba on Friday. Ekedayen attributed the reported N400 billion reduction to what he described as the Oborevwori administration’s prudent financial management and responsible use of public resources. He said: “We have been able to reduce our legacy debt from N463 billion to N63 billion. We are also working towards clearing the outstanding balance by the first quarter of 2027. “This achievement reflects the commitment of this administration to prudent financial management and responsible utilisation of public resources.” The commissioner said the state government would prioritise roads and other critical infrastructure in the proposed 2027 budget, citing their importance to economic growth and improved access to communities. He said the state’s expenditure structure currently allocated about 70 per cent to capital projects and 30 per cent to recurrent expenditure, adding that the government intended to sustain the emphasis on capital development in the next budget. The Asagba of Asaba, Prof. Epiphany Azinge, called for greater citizens’ participation in the budget preparation process, while commending the state government for its reported budget performance. Azinge said residents and other stakeholders should be given opportunities to contribute to decisions on projects and programmes that directly affect their communities. Meanwhile, civil society organisations at the engagement welcomed plans by the Delta State House of Assembly to introduce legislation regulating housing issues. They said appropriate legislation would help address challenges in the housing sector and provide a framework for improved regulation. item.title: Customs deploys AI tools to tackle fake news, online scams
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has begun deploying artificial intelligence and digital data-tracking tools to combat fake news and online scams capable of damaging its public image. The Comptroller-General of Customs, Adewale Adeniyi, disclosed this at the recently concluded NECCIPR Roundtable 2026 in Lagos. He was represented by the Service’s National Public Relations Officer, Deputy Comptroller Abdullahi Maiwada. Adeniyi said it was important for the Service to ensure that members of the public understood the reasons behind its policies, operations and enforcement activities. Speaking on the theme, “Algorithm Influence and Public Relations,” Maiwada said artificial intelligence had become increasingly important to Customs operations, including risk management and strategic communication. He explained that the technology was being used to assess risks associated with imported goods, classify consignments according to their risk levels and guide appropriate Customs interventions. According to him, AI can also analyse public sentiment and provide insights into how people perceive the activities of the Service. Maiwada said Customs was using available digital platforms to establish facts and working with other relevant agencies to identify and apprehend those responsible for spreading misleading information. He said: “The role of AI cannot be overemphasised, especially within our operations. Over the years, AI has been deployed in our core operational duties as well as strategic communication. “AI has also been deployed to aid risk management, which involves assessment of the risks in imported items so that they can be categorised according to their different levels of risk to enable appropriate Customs interventions.” Earlier, the convener of the NECCIPR Roundtable 2026, Nkechi Ali-Balogun, said the event was founded on the belief that public relations professionals should not only manage messages but also play a leading role in shaping national discourse. She said this year’s theme examined the growing influence of algorithms and artificial intelligence on public opinion and the flow of information. “When machines decide what we see, who is really shaping the Nigerian mind? Who now controls the flow of information that shapes what Nigerians believe? We live in a rapidly changing world, powered by AI, where a single algorithm can shape political narratives, throw out conspiracy theories, and dictate what millions read, believe, and share,” Ali-Balogun said. Adeboye spoke at a monthly special thanksgiving service and prayer session organised for social media influencers, creative industry practitioners, content creators and drama ministers at the church’s national headquarters, Throne of Grace Parish, Ebute-Metta, Lagos. He said media practitioners and content creators had a responsibility to investigate claims before disseminating them, noting that unverified reports could mislead the public. The cleric used the occasion to address two claims about him that had circulated in the media. He denied protesting against former President Goodluck Jonathan, explaining that a widely circulated photograph of him in white and green attire carrying a placard was taken during a prayer walk in 2020. According to him, the walk was organised in compliance with an instruction from the Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, for churches to hold prayer walks in their neighbourhoods. “It is true I carried a placard. It was a prayer walk. CAN said we should do a prayer walk near our churches. That is what I did in Ebute Meta. A walk is a walk,” he said. item.title: 325 People Arrested At Palestine Action Protest — UK Police
item.description: British police on Sunday said they had arrested 325 people at a London protest in support of Palestine Action the previous day, ahead of a court appeal over the government’s contentious ban of the group. Demonstrators staged a “mass action” outside the US embassy ahead of the Supreme Court holding a two-day hearing from Wednesday on the UK government’s July 2025 decision to outlaw Palestine Action under anti-terror legislation. The United States also designated Palestine Action as “terrorist” in August, as the administration of President Donald Trump intensifies its campaign against left-wing movements. The British designation puts the group on a blacklist that also includes entities like Palestinian militants Hamas, and made membership of, or support for, Palestine Action a crime punishable by up to 14 years in prison. Pro-Palestinian activists and supporters stage a protest in support of the proscribed group Palestine Action outside the US Embassy in London, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP) It has resulted in more than 4,000 people, including many senior citizens and Holocaust survivors, being arrested for showing their support for the group, according to campaigners and police tallies. “In total, 325 people were arrested yesterday,” London’s Metropolitan Police said in an update Sunday. “The vast majority of arrests — 320 — were for expressing support for a proscribed organisation under the Terrorism Act.” A smaller number of protesters also rallied outside the US consulate in the Scottish capital Edinburgh on Saturday, but no arrests were made there at the time. A pro-Palestinian activist holds a placard during a protest in support of the proscribed group Palestine Action outside the US Embassy in London, on October 31, 2026. The United States also designated Palestine Action as “terrorist” in August, as the administration of President Donald Trump intensifies its campaign against left-wing movements. The British designation puts the group on a blacklist that also includes entities like Palestinian militants Hamas, and made membership of, or support for, Palestine Action a crime punishable by up to 14 years in prison. Pro-Palestinian activists and supporters stage a protest in support of the proscribed group Palestine Action outside the US Embassy in London, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP) It has resulted in more than 4,000 people, including many senior citizens and Holocaust survivors, being arrested for showing their support for the group, according to campaigners and police tallies. “In total, 325 people were arrested yesterday,” London’s Metropolitan Police said in an update Sunday. “The vast majority of arrests — 320 — were for expressing support for a proscribed organisation under the Terrorism Act.” A smaller number of protesters also rallied outside the US consulate in the Scottish capital Edinburgh on Saturday, but no arrests were made there at the time. A pro-Palestinian activist holds a placard during a protest in support of the proscribed group Palestine Action outside the US Embassy in London, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP) “Enquiries are ongoing to identify people seen wearing t-shirts and holding banners showing support for a proscribed organisation,” Police Scotland said in a statement shared with AFP on Sunday. “Evidence is being reviewed and further action will be taken as appropriate.” The post 325 People Arrested At Palestine Action Protest — UK Police appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Enugu APC urges residents to verify political claims
item.description: By Dennis Agbo The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Enugu State has urged residents to exercise caution when receiving and sharing political information ahead of the 2027 general elections. The APC Campaign Council’s Spokesperson and Director of Public Communications, Steve Oruruo, made the appeal in a statement titled, “Unmasking the Alarmism of NDC: A Clarion Call for Enugu’s Extra Vigilance.” Oruruo referred to public discussions surrounding the management of Amadeo Event Centre and a proposed town hall meeting involving the New Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi. He said the disagreement over the use of the facility was a matter involving the parties to a private agreement and urged political stakeholders to avoid drawing conclusions about the involvement of the state government without verified information. The APC spokesperson also called on residents to verify reports, particularly those circulating on social media, before accepting or sharing them. He said political discussions ahead of the 2027 elections should focus on candidates’ ideas, policies and capacity to deliver good governance. Oruruo further highlighted the development programmes of Governor Peter Mbah’s administration, expressing confidence that the government’s record would feature prominently in the electoral contest. He urged Ndi Enugu to remain vigilant, promote issue-based political engagement and assess the proposals and records of political parties as the state approaches the 2027 general elections.
